narrative.overview: A bright, evidence-first operations desk built around a persistent queue, deterministic findings, and a bounded explanation workspace. Familiar blue-aqua confidence supports the work, while ClaimGuard's citations and audit-first composition create the identity.
keyCharacteristics: Navy structure, blue action, aqua evidence

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: Aqua is reserved for evidence, citations, provenance, and the visual path between a finding and its source.

rules.name: The Operational Gradient Rule
rules.body: Gradients are prohibited behind claim data, findings, tables, inputs, and corrective actions.

rules.name: The Data Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Claim amounts, dates, counts, and identifiers use tabular numerals so rows remain visually stable.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If every panel casts a shadow, the hierarchy has failed. Use borders and spacing first.

dos: Do keep queue, findings, and explanation visible together on wide screens.
Do show deterministic evidence before AI prose and attach every factual model statement to an evidence ID.
Do design loading, empty, failure, long-content, keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion states.
donts: Don't build a generic AI dashboard that leads with chat instead of the operator's queue.
Don't use marketing-style gradients, oversized hero metrics, or decorative glass effects inside operational workflows.
Don't create a literal Velodoc clone or use another company's private assets, copy, or proprietary identity.
Don't imply that the AI can adjudicate, submit, or alter a deterministic claim outcome.
